headline: A soft start is likely after Wall Street fell 1% overnight, with GIFT Nifty about 0.5% lower. But foreign funds have bought for six days straight, so a small dip looks more likely than the end of the rally.

mood.label: Mixed
mood.why: The dashboard's checks lean bullish (bias about +56, 3 of 4 steps agree), but the night brought weak global news. Overnight data as of 08:46 IST.

key_points.text: Overnight, the US S&P 500 fell **1%** to its lowest close since July, and most Asian markets are lower this morning. GIFT Nifty was about 122 points lower near 25,256 at 8 am.
FIIs (foreign funds) bought **₹4,195 crore** of Indian shares yesterday, their sixth buying day in a row. That brings November to about ₹88,000 crore.
My call: a **lower open, then a range** between about 25,000 and 25,500, not a deep fall. Confidence is medium.
Nvidia's results beat forecasts after the US close, and US futures are up slightly. This may calm the tech selling that hit Indian IT shares in the US overnight.
Markets now expect the US Fed to raise rates. The dollar is at a 1-year high, and the Fed's meeting notes come out tonight at **00:30 IST**.

sections.title: What changed overnight
sections.summary: The night brought mildly worse news, which works against yesterday's small rise. The only real comfort is Nvidia's strong results.

points.text: GIFT Nifty (a Nifty contract that trades overnight) was at about **25,256** at 8 am, roughly 0.5% below Nifty's close of 25,387. This points to a lower open.
US stocks fell on AI-chip and software selling: the S&P 500 lost **1.03%** and the Nasdaq 0.74%. The US fear gauge (VIX) jumped 11% to 25.5.

Nvidia's revenue of $115.8 billion beat the $109.1 billion forecast, and its shares rose about 2% after hours. S&P 500 futures are **up 0.2%** today, but still about 0.5% below where they stood when India closed.
Asia is mostly lower this morning: Hong Kong **−1.0%**, Taiwan −0.7%, China −0.3%, Japan −0.3%, and Korea flat.
Indian shares listed in the US were split. Infosys fell **−2.0%** and Wipro −2.8%, so IT could be weak. ICICI Bank rose +1.1%, and the US-listed India fund rose +0.7%.
Brent crude barely moved (about $92.9, +0.2%), and the rupee was steady at 93.47 per dollar. Gold fell **1.5%** to a 1-year low, a sign that investors are less scared.

sections.title: Bounce or continuation?
sections.summary: After a 10% run in November, I expect a small pullback at the open, with buyers stepping in near 25,000. Confidence is medium.

points.text: Signs of a pullback: weak global markets, the dollar at a 1-year high, and Nifty sitting right at its last swing high of **25,424**. It is also 5.9% above its 20-day average, which is stretched.
FIIs are buying shares in cash but quietly adding bets on a fall in index futures. Their long share slipped to **33%** from 37% on 12 November, and they bought more puts (insurance against a fall).
Signs the rally holds: six straight days of FII cash buying, crude about **15% lower** than a month ago, a firmer rupee, and option sellers building a floor at 25,000.
This suggests the dip gets bought, but a big push higher is unlikely today. I'd be wrong on the downside if Nifty closes **below 25,000**, and wrong on the upside if it closes above 25,500.

sections.title: The big picture
sections.summary: The dashboard's trend checks are clearly positive, and only the put-call ratio is neutral.

points.text: Price trend: Nifty is above its 20-, 50- and 200-day averages and is making higher highs and higher lows. That gives the full score of **+2**.
Futures: the price rose and open contracts rose 3.4%. That means new buyers came in (**+1.25**).
Option chain: sellers are writing puts at 24,800–25,100, which builds a floor at **25,000**. Calls are piling up at 25,500, which is the ceiling.
The put-call ratio (bets on a fall compared with bets on a rise) is **1.12**, a normal level. India VIX is 15.5 and falling, so fear is moderate (68th percentile of the past year).

sections.title: What big investors are doing
sections.summary: Foreign funds are buying heavily while Indian funds sell. That clash is the key story of November.

points.text: FIIs bought a net **₹4,195 crore** in cash yesterday, which counts as a big day by the dashboard's rule (₹3,000 crore or more). They have bought about ₹88,363 crore so far this month.
Domestic funds (DIIs) bought only ₹197 crore yesterday, and they have sold about **₹52,411 crore** this month. They are taking profits into the rally.
News reports say foreign money is moving out of expensive US AI stocks into India, which some see as a **non-AI market**. Cheaper crude has also helped.
FII index-futures long share is **33%**, up from 11% on 2 November. That is a big swing, but it slipped slightly yesterday, so the bets on a fall are no longer being closed.

sections.title: What the world is telling India
sections.summary: Cheap oil and a firm rupee help India, but a strong dollar and Fed rate-hike fears are the main threats.

points.text: Brent crude is about **$93**, down 15% in a month. India imports most of its oil, so this eases prices and the import bill.
The dollar index is at a **1-year high** (103.6). A strong dollar usually pulls money out of markets like India.
Six-month US Treasury bills pay **4.41%**, above the Fed's 3.88% rate. That gap rose by 0.15 points this week, which means markets expect a rate hike.
The US 10-year bond rate is high at **5.09%** but flat overnight. The dashboard's macro check reads Mixed: 3 bad signals and 4 good ones.

sections.title: Company results
sections.summary: No major Nifty results today, so stock-specific news matters more.

points.text: Eicher Motors (Nifty 50) reported revenue up 20% and profit up **15%**, which the dashboard reads as in line.
Manappuram Finance's revenue rose 56% and profit rose **77%**. Ashok Leyland's revenue rose 35%, but profit rose only 9%.
Fairfax plans to sell its whole **13.25%** stake in IIFL Finance through a block deal at ₹611 per share (about ₹3,454 crore). Large sales like this can weigh on a share price.
BlackRock reportedly raised its Axis Bank stake to about 5%, and HCLTech signed an AI partnership with Cohere. I couldn't confirm the exact Axis share count.

sections.title: What could change the picture
sections.summary: The Fed and the monthly expiry are the next tests, followed by India GDP and the RBI.

points.text: Fed meeting notes come out tonight at **00:30 IST**. Talk of more hikes would lift the dollar and could slow FII buying.
Monthly F&O expiry is on **23 November**, and markets are shut on 24 November. Expiry week can bring sharp swings around 25,000 and 25,500.
India GDP data comes on 30 November and the RBI rate decision on **4 December**. The Fed decides on 10 December.
The bullish read breaks if FIIs turn into sellers for two or more days, or if Nifty closes below **25,000**.

levels.note: A close above 25,500 would mean call sellers have given up and the rally is extending. A close below 25,000 would break the main floor and point to a deeper pullback.

watch.text: Opening gap: how much of GIFT Nifty's 0.5% drop shows up, and whether buyers step in.
IT shares after the falls in Infosys and Wipro US listings, and whether Nvidia's beat helps tech.
Banks: Bank Nifty hit a record yesterday. Watch whether it holds as FII buying continues.
Provisional FII/DII cash figures. A seventh straight FII buying day would support the trend.
US Fed meeting notes. Tough talk on rates would be bad for tomorrow's open.

bottom_line: The trend is up, and the dashboard's bias score is about +56 (bullish, medium conviction). Foreign funds are the main buyers. Overnight news is mildly negative: Wall Street fell, Asia is lower and GIFT Nifty points to a 0.5% weaker start. My read is a dip within a rising market, likely held around 25,000 to 25,500, rather than a turn lower. The main risk is a stronger dollar and Fed rate-hike fears, which could stop the foreign buying that drives this rally.
